_readme: Drop a photograph in this folder named after the event id, e.g. kedar13.webp,
then add its credit here and run `node build.js`. The build inlines it as a
data URI and the slide switches from the drawn illustration to the photograph,
with the credit line you give below printed under it.
Event ids: latur, odisha99, tsunami04, mumbai05, kedar13, hw15, chennai15,
kerala18, josh23, wayanad24.
Per-entry fields:
credit    required — who took it. No credit, no photograph.
licence   required — the licence it is published under.
source    optional — where the file came from.
verified  optional — false marks an attribution that has NOT been checked
against the source file page. The photograph still renders, but
its caption says so and the build prints a reminder. Set it true
once you have opened the file page and confirmed the line above.
w, h      optional — the pixel size, so the markup can reserve the box and
the hero can skip a source too small to fill it.
tone      optional — the image's dominant colour, painted behind it while
it decodes so nothing flashes.
Only use images you have the right to publish. Public-domain government
imagery (ISRO, NRSC, NASA, NOAA, NDRF, PIB) and Creative Commons photographs
on Wikimedia Commons are the usual sources; both require the attribution below
to be filled in accurately. A slide with no entry here keeps its illustration,
which is labelled as one — an unattributed photograph presented as documentary
is the one thing this project will not do.
NOT SHIPPED, DELIBERATELY: the supplied Latur 1993 photograph shows a casualty
in the rubble. This platform's own rule for the memorial is that it shows the
ground and the weather and never the dying, and a photograph of a dead person
on an autoplaying public slideshow breaks it. That slide keeps its illustration.
